relevance_note: Case report of one patient with Danon disease and a LAMP2 variant: 'the patient was hemizygous for a frameshift mutation in the LAMP2 gene, confirming the diagnosis of Danon disease'.
method_note: Single-patient case report, read in full and transcribed by hand into a small Python builder; no tables in the paper. The proband is labelled 'patient' (rule 5). The two previously published boys of reference ^1 (Danon 1981) are included under the v4 in-passing rule because the Discussion gives sex, age (16 years) and features for them; they are labelled 'ref ^1 patient' and 'ref ^1 patient 2' and their features are stated jointly for both ('two unrelated 16-year-old boys with mental retardation, cardiomegaly, and proximal skeletal myopathy'). Maron et al. (ref ^3) seven-patient cohort, ref ^9 subjects and refs ^11/^12 are described only at group level and get no rows. The variant is printed twice in protein notation only: 'L141VfsX9' (Case Presentation, used as variant_original_string) and 'p.Leu141ValfsX9' (Discussion, used as protein_hgvs_as_stated); no cDNA, transcript or genomic coordinates are printed ('Xq24' is a cytoband, not recorded as coordinates). Ages: the patient presented at 15 years; the age at the Danon diagnosis and at last evaluation are not given as numbers (diagnosis came after an SVT episode 'Two years later', last report 'At two years following the diagnosis'), so both are 'not reported'. Normal findings (D-27): 'His skeletal muscle strength and muscle tone were normal throughout' recorded as muscle weakness and abnormal muscle tone excluded, and used to exclude the checklist item proximal muscle weakness (skeletal myopathy). 'no significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction' recorded as excluded. 'mild cognitive delay' mapped to the cognitive-impairment checklist item only; developmental delay left not reported. 'There was not a family history of cardiomyopathies, arrhythmias, or sudden cardiac death' is not parental testing; inheritance not reported. The paper's 'presumptive diagnosis was sarcomeric HCM' was later revised; it is not recorded as a feature. No internal contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: oral beta-blocker; implantable cardioverter-defibrillator; radiofrequency ablation of two accessory pathways; antiarrhythmic agents being titrated; not yet considered for heart transplantation
span: the patient was started on an oral β-blocker and received an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator
The patient then underwent radiofrequency ablation of two accessory pathways within the tricuspid valve annulus.
Antiarrhythmic agents were being titrated with the hope of controlling symptoms.
The patient had not yet been considered for a heart transplantation.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: genetic testing (hemizygous LAMP2 frameshift) confirming a clinical suspicion raised by WPW with massive LVH
span: an association between WPW and massive LVH introduced a suspicion for Danon syndrome
Subsequent genetic testing revealed that the patient was hemizygous for a frameshift mutation in the LAMP2 gene, confirming the diagnosis of Danon disease.
